In China, there once lived a father, his four sons, and three daughters-in-law. His three older sons had married within a few months of each other and all with young women from the same village. Their new father-in-law's wife had died a few years before and having no mother-in-law with them in their new home, and being lonesome and homesick for their former families, they constantly asked the old man for permission to visit their former village. For you see, those were the days when young women, after they married and moved into the homes of their new husbands, needed permission to leave the household. In the case of sentences like this where the sentence takes an Interrogative form in Direct Speech, "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc. in Indirect Speech is changed into "said" in Direct Speech.

In Direct speech, the verb is always placed before the subject, unlike in Indirect Speech.

When changing these types of sentences from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech, "Whom" becomes "Who".

For example:

Ravi asked me whom I had visited this afternoon. (Indirect Speech)

Ravi said to me, "Who have you visited in the afternoon?" (Direct Speech)

The tense of the Indirect Speech is in the Past Perfect tense. So, the tense in the Direct Speech will be in the Present Perfect tense.

The following things in the sentence will change when changed from Indirect Speech to Direct Speech:

Indirect SpeechDirect Speech
askedsaid to
whomWho
she hadhave you

Therefore, the correct answer is: (b) Susan said to Selena, "Who have you asked to remove the chair?"

questions.solution_en:
Melancholic - expressing feelings of sadness.

The antonym of 'melancholic' is 'exuberant', meaning full of energy and excitement. Hence, (d) is the correct answer.

questions.q_en:
Select the meaning of the idiom in bold and italics.

Sometimes he decides when he is beside himself.
questions.solution_en:
The meaning of the idiom 'beside himself' is 'out of his/her mind'. Among the options, 'out of mind' is the correct option that matches the meaning of the given idiom.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).
